title: Average True Range (ATR) Technical Indicator Guide
author: Investopedia Technical Analysis Team
content:
Average True Range (ATR) is a market volatility indicator used in technical analysis. Introduced by J. Welles Wilder Jr. in his 1978 book 'New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems', the ATR measures market volatility by decomposing the entire range of an asset price for that period.

True Range calculation is defined as the greatest of the following three values:
1. Current High minus current Low (High - Low)
2. Absolute value of current High minus previous Close (|High - Close_prev|)
3. Absolute value of current Low minus previous Close (|Low - Close_prev|)

ATR does not indicate price trend direction, but rather the degree of price volatility. Traders frequently utilize a 14-period ATR to gauge suitable Stop Loss placement (e.g., 1.5x or 2.0x ATR buffer) and position sizing thresholds to avoid getting stopped out by normal market noise.
